title: Cartier Gysin normalization in the signed relative Kummer model
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $n\geq1$, $m=\ell^n$, and $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/m\mathbf Z$. Let $X$ be a Noetherian excellent regular affine scheme with $\ell$ invertible [def-exc-excellent-ring, def-weil-regular-scheme], and let $f\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a nonzerodivisor such that the effective Cartier divisor $D=V(f)$ is regular [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. Write $i:D\hookrightarrow X$ and $j:U=X-D\hookrightarrow X$. Work on small etale derived categories with $\Lambda_X(1)=\mu_{m,X}$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist]. Let $\kappa(f)\in H^1(U,\mu_m)$ be the class of the $\mu_m$-torsor of $m$-th roots of $f|_U$, equivalently the Kummer connecting class [lem-amb-kummer-any-base, lem-sc-torsor-h1]. Put $H^q_D(X,\mu_m)=H^q(R\Gamma_D(X,\mu_m))$ [def-pur-etale-derived-supported-sections]. Fix the signed relative realization of [def-amb-relative-etale-cohomology, lem-pur-divisor-torsor-boundary-signs]: on an injective resolution $J$ its differential is $D(a,b)=(da,\operatorname{res}(a)-db)$ on $J^q(X)\oplus J^{q-1}(U)$ and its localization boundary $\partial:H^1(U,\mu_m)\to H^2_D(X,\mu_m)$ is represented by $b\mapsto(0,-b)$. Use the Yoneda convention for the supported Chern class of a line bundle $B$ with an invertible section $s$ on $U$: its degree-one supported extension has fibre over the supported generator equal to the frame torsor of $B$, with the specified frame $s$ sent to zero, and its degree-two class is the Yoneda product with the Kummer extension. This specifies the Chern normalization allowed in Expose XVI, Definition 1.1 and its sign footnote. Use the Kummer-normalized regular-immersion class $\eta_{i,n}$ of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus]; in the notation for the absolute Gysin map [lem-per-absolute-gysin-purity], normalize $\operatorname{Cl}_i(1)[2]=\eta_{i,n}$. This specifies the normalization, which the bare existence of a canonical isomorphism does not determine. Under the supported-Hom and closed-adjunction identifications [lem-amb-closed-support-hom], this morphism $\operatorname{Cl}_i(1)[2]:\Lambda_D\to i^!\Lambda_X(1)[2]$ corresponds to
$$-\partial\kappa(f)\in H^2_D(X,\mu_m).$$
The minus sign is the value of the normalized Yoneda/ILO class after the codimension-one Kummer pin is expressed in this signed relative realization.

source.place: Expose XVI, sections 2.1–2.3: Definition 2.1.1, Definitions 2.2.2.5 and 2.2.2.7 (rank one), Definition 2.3.1; comparison with the explicitly specified signed relative Kummer realization. The signed-relative comparison is agent-stated, not a verbatim assertion of XVII Proposition 2.4.2.1(a).

proof.text: If $D$ is empty, the supported groups and $\Lambda_D$ are zero, so the assertion holds. Henceforth suppose $D$ is nonempty. Put $I=f\mathcal O_X$. Multiplication by the nonzerodivisor $f$ is an isomorphism $\mathcal O_X\to I$, $a\mapsto af$, giving a global frame $e=f$. At a point of $D$, $f$ lies in the maximal ideal; the local quotient by $f$ is nonzero. Thus $(f)$ is a regular sequence in the precise convention of [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], on neighbourhoods of the divisor. The map $\mathcal O_D\to I/I^2$, $\bar a\mapsto af\bmod f^2$, is an isomorphism: $af=f^2b$ implies $a=fb$ by cancellation. This is a codimension-one regular immersion with conormal bundle $E=I/I^2$ of rank one. The Cartier terminology is [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]; no smoothness over a field is asserted.

Compute the degree-one supported extension defining $c_1(I,1_U)$ in the prescribed convention. Its frame torsor is the one of [lem-sc-line-bundle-torsor]. On $U$, $1_U=f^{-1}e$. If $a:\mathbf G_m\to E_I$ is the extension inclusion and $F$ its equivariant frame map, then $F(1_U)=0$ gives $F(e)=a(f)$, writing the group law additively. This is an equality of sections on $U$, not a choice of sign. The global frame $e$ lifts the section $1$ of $\mathbf Z_X$ to $F(e)$ in $E_I$. Therefore $E_I$ is the pushout of the open-closed sequence of [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact] along $1\mapsto f|_U$: the map from $\mathbf G_m\oplus\mathbf Z_X$ sends $(g,n)$ to $a(g)+nF(e)$, and on $j_!\mathbf Z_U$ the relation is $(-f,1)=0$. It is an isomorphism on the kernel $\mathbf G_m$ and on the quotient $i_*\mathbf Z_D$, hence on the middle sheaf by exactness (lift a local quotient section and then compare in the kernel). All frames here belong to $I$, rather than its dual.

source.place: XVI 2.1, the pair (I,1_U), with the specified Yoneda normalization; explicit frame calculation

proof.text: In [lem-per-supported-yoneda-localization] take $G_1=\mu_m$, $G_2=G_3=\mathbf G_m$, the Kummer sequence [lem-amb-kummer-any-base], and $h=f|_U$. Exactness applies because $m=\ell^n$ is invertible. The ordinary connecting class is $\kappa(f)$, equivalently the torsor of $m$-th roots: a local lift of $f$ is just such a root, and the differences of two lifts are their ratios in $\mu_m$, as in [lem-sc-torsor-h1]. Step 2 identifies the first extension with $e_h$. Its Yoneda product with the Kummer extension is, by the Chern convention in the statement, $c_1(I,1_U)$. The cited signed comparison therefore gives $c_1(I,1_U)=\partial\kappa(f)$, where the localization boundary is exactly $b\mapsto(0,-b)$. In particular the termwise relative coefficient connecting map is not substituted for this Yoneda product.

source.place: XVI 1.1 sign footnote and 2.1; signed Yoneda comparison supplied by lem-per-supported-yoneda-localization

proof.text: Use the Cartier class $c_{D,\Lambda}$ of [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer] with $N=m$ and $A=\Lambda$. Its supported boundary is defined by [def-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer-boundary], not by that theorem's proof. By [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle], $L=\mathcal O_X(D)=I^\vee$. Its global dual frame is $e=f^{-1}$ and its divisor section is $s_D=fe$. In the frame torsor of [lem-sc-line-bundle-torsor], write $F$ for the equivariant map into the supported extension and $a$ for its kernel inclusion. Since $F(s_D)=0$, equivariance gives $F(e)=a(f^{-1})$ on $U$. Thus the pushout calculation of step 2, using [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact], now gives $e_{f^{-1}}$: the map $(g,k)\mapsto a(g)+kF(e)$ has the pushout relation and is an isomorphism on kernel and quotient, hence on the middle sheaf by the same local lifting argument. The definition requires its Yoneda product with the exact Kummer extension of [lem-amb-kummer-any-base]; for $A=\mathbf Z/m$ the roots scalar map is the identity. Apply [lem-per-supported-yoneda-localization] to $h=f^{-1}$. The root torsor has class $\kappa(f^{-1})=-\kappa(f)$: inversion on roots identifies it with the inverse torsor, whose class is the negative by [lem-sc-torsor-h1]. Consequently the defining supported class of $c_{D,\Lambda}$ is $\partial\kappa(f^{-1})=-\partial\kappa(f)$.

source.place: Tag 03PL, lemma-kummer-sequence; statement-level Yoneda specification of def-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer-boundary, computed with the dual frame and the signed localization comparison

proof.text: The codimension-one clause of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] states that $\eta_{i,n}$ is the closed adjoint of $c_{D,\Lambda}$; step 1 verifies its regular-immersion hypothesis and $m=\ell^n$ is exactly its coefficient ring. By [lem-amb-closed-support-hom], $c_{D,\Lambda}$ corresponds to the supported class computed in step 4. Transposing across the same closed adjunction and using the stipulated normalization $\operatorname{Cl}_i(1)[2]=\eta_{i,n}$ gives the displayed value $-\partial\kappa(f)$. This uses the statement-level Kummer pin and the Yoneda calculation for $f^{-1}$, not a sign inferred from the bare existence of absolute purity or from the proof of [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer]. Steps 3 and 4 also give the consistency check $c_1^{\mathrm{Yon}}(\mathcal O_X(D),s_D)=-c_1^{\mathrm{Yon}}(I,1_U)$ under the supported-Hom identification, as expected for the dual line bundle.

source.place: XVI Definition 1.1 sign footnote and Definition 2.3.1; explicit Kummer pin of lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus

proof_origin.place: XVI Definition 1.1 (sign footnote) and 2.1 for the Yoneda Chern normalization; the codimension-one pin uses the definition-level supported Kummer product for (O(D),s_D), computed at h=f^{-1}, giving -∂κ(f).
